A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VSRM work, with readable text, equations, eight tables and six figures across 11 pages. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements. The separate supplementary file mentioned in both is unavailable; this comparison covers the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original video super-resolution results, component ablations and complexity measurements in Tables 2–8, plus qualitative and receptive-field results in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results in Tables 2–8 and Figures 5–6.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same dual aggregation blocks, scanning procedures, temporal gated network, deformable cross-Mamba alignment and frequency-domain loss. No algorithmic or architectural revision is documented.

E1.justification: Both train on REDS and Vimeo-90K and evaluate ×4 video super-resolution on REDS4, Vimeo-90K-T and Vid4. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains EDVR, VSR-T, VRT, BasicVSR++, RVRT, PSRT-recurrent and IART. Comparator membership also matches in the ablation, complexity and visual comparisons. Newly inserted citations [51, 52] are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported REDS4 split, bicubic degradation, ×4 scale, PSNR/SSIM metrics and input-frame/model configurations are unchanged. No evaluation protocol or experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: Tables 3–7 retain the same backbone, alignment, scanning, TGFN and frequency-loss ablations. The qualitative examples and effective receptive-field analysis in Figures 5–6 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 retain all numerical entries, and Figures 5–6 retain the same findings. For example, Table 2's VSRM 16/7-frame row reports the same PSNR values of 33.11, 38.33 and 28.44 dB on REDS4, Vimeo-90K-T and Vid4.

T1.justification: The state-space definitions and discretization in Section 3 and method/loss formulations in Equations (4)–(15) are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same first-Mamba-for-VSR claim, proposed component contributions and state-of-the-art performance claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal modeling, adaptive alignment, frequency-loss benefits and receptive fields remain unchanged. Section 5.4 retains the same complexity tradeoff discussion, with no new limitations or applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The disclosed pretrained SpyNet, loss weights, epsilon and RTX A6000 48GB runtime hardware remain unchanged. The new GPU-support acknowledgment identifies a supporting organization but adds no technical settings or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly cites [51], Trans2UNet for nuclei segmentation, and [52], channel-partitioned windowed attention for single-image super-resolution, in transformer-related statements. Both works were already in v2's bibliography; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adjusts grouped author-email formatting and adds an Acknowledgments section covering funding, scholarship and GPU support. The scientific prose and main section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is displayed slightly smaller, and text, equations and tables reflow within the existing layout; Equation (13), for example, moves from page 6 to page 5. Figure content, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The methods, experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged. New acknowledgments improve attribution, while contact formatting and layout receive modest adjustments. The newly placed citations concern adjacent tasks and add no substantive VSR comparison. These limited changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
